item.title: [New] Two identity-library CVEs published on 15 October: Microsoft Identity Web elevation of privilege and MSAL for Node.js information disclosure
item.description:
These are libraries inside your own line-of-business apps, so no Windows or Office patch covers them; an app that authorizes on a claim the attacker can influence is an access-control flaw in software you own.

Entra · Ask application owners which web APIs use Microsoft.Identity.Web and which Node.js services use @azure/msal-node, and get the fixed package versions from the two MSRC pages into their next release.

item.title: [New] Entra may now show a risk-based CAPTCHA from Arkose Labs before sending an SMS or placing a voice call for sign-in
item.description:
A user who cannot finish an SMS sign-in may be blocked by a proxy or web filter that drops the Arkose Labs domains, not by an attack. It also confirms that SMS and voice are being abused enough for Microsoft to gate them — another reason to retire them.

Entra · Add the Arkose Labs domains Microsoft lists to your proxy allow list, brief the service desk on the new dialog, and use it as a prompt to move remaining SMS and voice users to Authenticator or passkeys.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Enterprise app 'Activation status' is now documented: Deactivated can mean tenant sign-in off, the app registration deactivated, or Microsoft disabling the app
item.description:
During a consent-phishing response the label 'Deactivated' is ambiguous: an analyst who sees it may assume Microsoft has already disabled the app, or may re-enable sign-in and believe the app works again. Only the three properties tell which condition applies.

Entra · Update the consent-phishing playbook to read accountEnabled, isDisabled and disabledByMicrosoftStatus through Graph instead of trusting the portal label, and alert when disabledByMicrosoftStatus is set on any service principal in your tenant.

item.description:
The version that clears the 30 September floor itself leaves support on 23 October, so an upgrade aimed at 2.5.79.0 buys three weeks and then has to be done again.

Entra · deadline 2026-10-23 · Aim the September upgrade at a build later than 2.5.79.0 so it is one change window rather than two on a tier-0 server.

item.title: [New] ID Protection's atypical travel detection is now documented as real-time, not offline, and the 14-day learning period is gone from the page
item.description:
A real-time detection raises sign-in risk during the sign-in itself, so a risk-based Conditional Access policy can now challenge or block an atypical-travel sign-in instead of the user being flagged after the fact. Expect more MFA prompts and blocks attributed to unlikelyTravel, and a change in DetectionTimingType in AADUserRiskEvents.

Entra · Review sign-in-risk Conditional Access policies with this in mind, tell the service desk that travelling users may be challenged at sign-in, and trend unlikelyTravel by DetectionTimingType to see when your tenant moves (query in Hunting).

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] October security update switches NTLMv1-derived SSO credentials from audit to block on devices without Credential Guard
item.description:
A wave of Wi-Fi or VPN failures after Patch Tuesday will look like an outage or a credential attack. The temporary fix, BlockNtlmv1SSO = 0, re-enables a weak credential path; anyone who sets it fleet-wide without an expiry undoes the hardening.

Windows · Inventory 802.1X and VPN profiles that still use PEAP-MSCHAPv2 or EAP-MSCHAPv2 on Windows 11 24H2+ and Server 2025 without Credential Guard; plan the move to EAP-TLS; if you must return devices to audit mode, scope it by group, record an end date and watch Event ID 4024 until it stops.

item.title: [Due in 3 days] Entra sign-in pages start enforcing a Content Security Policy in mid-October; injected scripts stop running on login.microsoftonline.com
item.description:
Anything your organisation injects into the sign-in page — a password-manager or DLP browser extension, a session-recording or monitoring tool, a branding hack — stops running silently. The same header also blocks a malicious extension from scraping credentials there, which is the point.

Entra · deadline 2026-10-19 · Before 19 October, walk a sign-in on login.microsoftonline.com with the browser dev console open on a standard managed build and look for CSP violations in red; list every extension or tool that shows up and ask its vendor for a CSP-compliant version. Tell the help desk that a monitoring or SSO helper extension failing on the sign-in page after mid-October is expected.

item.title: [New] From 4 November every default user can create agent blueprints unless 'Users can create agent blueprints' is set to No
item.description:

Entra · Decide before 4 November: set 'Users can create agent blueprints' to No unless there is a business case, keep Agent ID Developer as the delegated path, and add agent blueprint creation by non-admins to the app-registration detections.

item.title: [New] Seven Graph permissions became grantable and two gained a delegated scope: the trusted-issuer list for federated identity credentials, Copilot spending policies and cross-tenant content migration
item.description:
AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.ReadWrite.All lets an app 'create, read, update, and delete the trusted federated credential issuers that can be used to restrict which identity providers must be used when configuring federated identity credentials', without a signed-in user: whoever holds it decides which external identity providers a workload identity in the tenant may trust. CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All can create and delete Copilot spending policies that, in Microsoft's words, 'may take effect immediately and restrict user spending', and CopilotCostManagement-UserData.Read.All reads 'any named user's Copilot credit balance' and usage by security group. Microsoft has published no documentation for any of the three families.

Graph · Nothing is granted by this change. Add the two application role IDs and nine delegated scope IDs from the Graph API tab to the consent watch list today, decline consent for AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.ReadWrite.All until Microsoft documents the feature, and run the first query in Hunting & actions to confirm none has been granted since 6 October.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Message trace through Graph can now return the status recalled, but only when the request asks for unknown enum members
item.description:
A script that reads message trace through Graph without the Prefer header receives unknownFutureValue for a recalled message, so a recall after a phishing report or a data-loss mistake looks like an unclassified row. With the header, recalled messages can be counted and tied to the investigation that triggered them.

Graph · Add the Prefer: include-unknown-enum-members header to message-trace collectors that use Graph and map the new value; no tenant setting changes.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Microsoft 365 Backup activity logs get a Graph API (beta): policy changes, offboarding and restore tasks readable with BackupRestore-Monitor.Read.All
item.description:
Pausing a backup policy or offboarding protection units is what an intruder does before destroying data, and until now those actions were visible only in the admin center view announced in MC1489931. A Graph endpoint makes them collectable: a scheduled read can raise backupPolicyPaused, policyLevelOffboarding and protectionUnitLevelOffboarding as events of their own.

Graph · If Microsoft 365 Backup is in use, grant BackupRestore-Monitor.Read.All to the collection application rather than a wider BackupRestore permission, and plan a rule on paused policies and offboarding; treat the schema as beta and subject to change.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Agent ID lifecycle policies (preview): Lifecycle Workflows can disable or delete agent identities that are inactive, have too few sponsors or were not reconfirmed
item.description:
This is the first Microsoft control that removes an agent identity nobody answers for, which is the population incident responders keep finding with standing access. It is also a new way for an identity to be disabled or deleted without an administrator doing it by hand: a production agent whose sponsor ignores a notification stops working, and the actor in the audit trail is the lifecycle service. The two LifecyclePolicies-AgentId Graph permissions Microsoft documented on 8 October are the programmatic side of the same feature.

Entra · Pilot with Specific agents as the scope and a fallback recipient the SOC can read, as the article itself recommends, before any tenant-wide policy; decide who may hold Lifecycle Workflows Administrator and AI Administrator, because either can now schedule deletion of agent identities.

item.title: [New] Pre-authenticated (tempauth) file URLs retire on 1 April 2027: Graph file APIs stop returning URLs with an embedded token, and a tenant control lets you test per application first
item.description:
A tempauth URL is a bearer credential in a link: whoever holds the URL reads the file with no further authentication for as long as it lives, and it travels through logs, proxies and tickets. Its retirement removes that exposure, and it also breaks every backup tool, migration tool, scanner and line-of-business script that stores, inspects or redeems such URLs or follows the 302 redirect. Applications that call SharePoint URLs directly afterwards need an Entra ID access token for the SharePoint resource, which also means their file access appears in sign-in logs where it did not before.

SharePoint · Ask the owners of backup, DLP, eDiscovery, migration and custom integrations whether they use Graph download, upload-session, copy, preview, thumbnail or version URLs; when the tenant control ships, opt a small set of application IDs in and watch for authentication failures before widening it. Record the vendors' support dates well before April 2027.

item.description:
A permission an application can hold unattended is a different risk from one exercised on behalf of a signed-in administrator, and this one writes a tenant-wide policy. The reference is ahead of the service principal here, so the first tenant grant will come after a ring deployment, with no announcement (inferred from the two sources disagreeing).

item.title: [New] Microsoft's Graph permissions reference documents 33 more permissions, among them the thirteen that delete users' authentication methods, four identity-diagnostic names and four Customer Lockbox names
item.description:
Every one of these names was already in this catalog, read from the service principal or from Microsoft's deployment map weeks before the page carried it, so nothing new became grantable today. What changed is that an approver can now look the name up, and that a consent review built from the documentation gains 33 rows it did not have. The delete-only family grants no read and no write, so a review that searches for ReadWrite on authentication methods still does not find it.

Graph · Add the 33 names and their identifiers to the consent-review list from the Graph API tab, then query app role assignments for the thirteen authentication-method delete roles and confirm that only a joiner-mover-leaver tool holds any of them.

item.title: [New] Entra Health Monitoring documents two new alert scenarios for AI agents: Agent ID interactive sign-ins and Agent ID autonomous sign-ins (preview)
